Two models per game. Football and college basketball: ESPN's power index (FPI/BPI) and an opponent-adjusted ratings model built only from games already played. NBA and NHL: the ratings model and each team's last 10 games.

A game gets a call only when both models land on the same side by at least the bar: 3 points in football, 4.5 in basketball, 5 win-probability points in hockey. One model alone is a WATCH, never a bet.
Automatic pass: the two models are 10+ points apart. Any model 7+ points from the market is a re-check warning, not a reason to bet.
Cash requires three things: both models agree, confidence 7.0+, and the past-games test shows that kind of pick won 53.5%+ over 200+ games. Otherwise it is PAPER: tracked and graded, $0.
L-1112-1 (your call, 11/12): no $25 single on midweek or small-conference college football. Those need 8.0+.
Units never change on their own: $50 at 8.0+, $25 at 7.0-7.9, $15 parlays, 2 tickets per game, $180 day cap, stop at -$150. Never chase.
The first line logged for a pick is the one it is graded on. Every pick is also compared with the closing line, so we can see whether we got a good number.
Line movement is used only as a price check, never as a reason to bet.
